items.quote: These procedures set out the process the University will follow to investigate Reports filed under the Sexualized Violence Prevention and Response Policy (“the Policy”).
items.reason: The policy has its own dedicated investigation procedures for reports.

items.quote: The University will create and maintain a Sexualized Violence website that provides information about the Policy as well as support and response options and an up-to-date list of Sexualized Violence Education opportunities.
items.reason: The policy commits to providing information about the policy on a website, but does not explicitly state the policy text itself will be publicly posted.

items.quote: There are generally three main process options after making a Disclosure to EQHR: (a) requesting no further action beyond keeping a record (see section 13); (b) requesting a Voluntary Process (see Appendix C – Voluntary Process Procedures); or (c) completing and filing a Report (see Appendix D – Procedures for Filing a Report).
items.reason: The policy outlines the general options for reporting but does not provide specific contact details like phone numbers or email addresses in the text.
The policy does not address whether a complainant's past sexual history can be raised or considered during the process.

items.quote: The Complainant and Respondent will not be required to meet as part of the investigation.
items.reason: The policy explicitly guarantees that the complainant and respondent will not be required to meet.

items.quote: University Community Members who are participating in a Voluntary Process, investigation, or review are free to speak about their own experiences but must not disclose information that they learn solely as a result of their participation in Policy processes, because this Personal Information belongs to another individual.
items.reason: The policy explicitly states that participants are free to speak about their own experiences.

items.quote: These additional relevant processes might include: (a) a grievance through their union; (b) a report of a crime directly to the police; (c) a human rights complaint to the BC Human Rights Tribunal; (d) a claim or complaint to WorkSafeBC; and/or (e) a civil suit.
items.reason: External options such as police and civil suits are mentioned, but the explicit right of the survivor to choose between them is not fully articulated.

items.quote: Hence, the University will not subject any individual who makes a Disclosure or Report or witnesses Sexualized Violence to disciplinary action for their personal use of alcohol or substance use occurring at or near the time of the incident(s).
items.reason: The policy provides a binding guarantee of amnesty for drug or alcohol use at the time of the incident.

items.quote: The Director will specify an expected timeline for the investigator to complete the investigation and submit the investigation report.
items.reason: Timelines for the overall investigation are discretionary and set on a case-by-case basis.

items.quote: The University may apply Interim Measures where the University believes it must act to protect a University Community Member’s health or safety or University property.
items.reason: The application of interim measures is discretionary.

items.quote: A University Activity includes but is not limited to: (a) in-person and online courses; (b) athletic events; (c) artistic performances; (d) placements (including co-op and practica); (e) meetings to further University business; (f) academic or professional conferences; and (g) academic or research field work.
items.reason: The policy's scope explicitly covers placements, including co-op and practica.

items.quote: Therefore, the Complainant is not entitled to know whether the Respondent was disciplined, or which corrective action was imposed.
items.reason: The complainant is informed of the outcome of the investigation, but is explicitly not entitled to know the specific disciplinary actions or sanctions imposed.

items.quote: This report will be publicly available online and will contain: (a) available statistics on Disclosures and Reports to EQHR (including available demographic details); (b) observed trends related to Sexualized Violence at the University; and (c) recommendations based on trends.
items.reason: The policy commits to publishing an annual report online containing statistics on disclosures and reports.

items.quote: In any event, the University will review the Policy at least once every three years, and when directed to do so by the provincial government.
items.reason: The policy mandates a review cycle of at least once every three years, which is longer than the two-year benchmark.
The policy does not mention a requirement for student representation on the policy review committee.

items.quote: General Counsel Office will compile and maintain a roster of investigators who: (a) are trained in Trauma-Informed investigation practices;
items.reason: The policy requires investigators on the roster to have trauma-informed training, but does not mandate it for all decision-makers.

items.quote: The University is committed to addressing and preventing Sexualized Violence by implementing and actively promoting awareness, education, and training programs in multiple formats and tailored to multiple audiences (see Appendix H – Sexualized Violence Education Framework).
items.reason: The policy commits to implementing prevention education and training programs for the university community.
